record.paper_title: Open problems in Euclidean Ramsey Theory
record.original_question: Call a finite subset X of some Euclidean space Ramsey if, for every number of colors r, every sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space colored with r colors contains a monochromatic congruent copy of X. A necessary condition stated in the source is that any Ramsey set must lie on the surface of a sphere in some dimension; such a set is called spherical. Is every spherical finite set Ramsey?

evidence.quote: any Ramsey set must lie on the surface of a sphere
Conjecture 5 ($1000). Every spherical set is Ramsey.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A finite subset X of a Euclidean space is called Ramsey if, for every positive integer r, there exists a positive integer N = N(X, r) such that for every r-coloring of the points of R^N there is a monochromatic subset congruent to X. A finite set is called spherical if it lies on the surface of some sphere in some Euclidean space (equivalently, all of its points are equidistant from some common center in their affine span). It is known that every Ramsey set must be spherical.

Question: Is every finite spherical subset of Euclidean space a Ramsey set?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that every spherical finite set is Ramsey (Graham's $1000 conjecture) remains open. Known Ramsey sets include simplices, vertex sets of regular polygons, and Platonic solids; Kříž showed that sets admitting a transitive soluble group action are Ramsey. Leader, Russell and Walters proposed a rival conjecture that the Ramsey sets are exactly subsets of transitive sets, and showed it is distinct from Graham's conjecture (some cyclic quadrilaterals are spherical but not subsets of any finite transitive set). Recent work (2024–2025) continues to investigate the conjecture without resolving it.

status_evidence.title: Transitive Sets in Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Leader, Russell, Walters)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a rival conjecture; notes that there exist spherical sets not contained in any finite transitive set.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains open; rival conjecture proposed.

status_evidence.title: Nearly all known Euclidean Ramsey sets are subsoluble
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work analyzing Ramsey sets, indicating the spherical-implies-Ramsey conjecture is still unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research without a resolution.

status_evidence.title: Euclidean Ramsey Theory (Graham)
status_evidence.snippet: Graham's survey presents the conjecture that every spherical set is Ramsey as open.
